title: Bridging Gaps in Hate Speech Detection: Meta-Collections and Benchmarks for Low-Resource Iberian Languages

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating performance disparities in hate speech detection by comparing F1 scores of LLMs (Llama 3.1, Nemo, multilingual BERT) in zero-shot, few-shot, and fine-tuned settings across high-resource (English) and low-resource Iberian languages and variants (European Spanish, European Portuguese, and Galician).

Analyzing the dataset composition to quantify the prevalence of sexism and misogyny using term frequency analysis, psycholinguistic profiling (emotion and pronoun usage), and topic modeling (BERTopic with t-SNE) to identify gender-based hate speech clusters.

Applying topic modeling (BERTopic) and semantic clustering to detect and map hate speech narratives and stereotypes targeting race, ethnicity, and immigration status within the multilingual meta-collection.
